key_insight: Sparse AFM scans can be expanded into a probabilistic ensemble of plant cell-wall microstructures, enabling uncertainty-aware prediction of effective elastic properties and macroscale tensile response.
engineering_relevance: This workflow offers a scalable way to translate limited nanoscale imaging into continuum-level mechanics for fibrous bio-materials, supporting more reliable design and interpretation under structural variability.
method: Use Stable Diffusion + LoRA to generate AFM-like synthetic microstructures from sparse scans.
Screen generated images with microfibril crossover count and crossover angle to preserve structural realism.
Map each microstructure to spatial Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio fields, then run strain-controlled FE homogenization and stochastic tensile simulations.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the synthetic ensemble through structural metrics and propagate it through homogenization and 20 stochastic tensile simulations, showing distributions of effective moduli, Poisson's ratio, and macroscale stress rather than a single deterministic value.
watch_item: Quantitative prediction still depends on calibrating the intensity-to-property mapping against nanomechanical measurements, so current results are a framework rather than a fully validated material model.
paper_title: From Sparse AFM Observations to Probabilistic Macroscale Mechanics: A Generative-Physics Framework for Plant Cell Walls
